title: تَابِعُ حِكَايَةِ الْقَرَنْدَلِيِّ الثَّالِثِ: الْفَارِسُ النُّحَاسِيُّ وَابْنُ الْجَوْهَرِيِّ
titleEn: The Third Qalandar's Tale, Continued: The Brass Horseman and the Jeweler's Son
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 105–110 (continuing directly from nights-14, whose text breaks off as the Third Qalandar opens his own tale), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the project’s own two-pass-plus-adjudication pipeline; the edition’s own OCR is unusable. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition’s — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor’s slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized automatically once this file is published, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 15 continues the Third Qalandar’s own tale without interruption. A voice in a dream sends him to dig up a brass bow and lead arrows and shoot down the horseman-and-horse automaton crowning the Black Mountain; he does, buries the bow as instructed, and is carried by a small copper skiff across ten days of open sea toward safety — only for the skiff itself to fling him into the water short of land, leaving him to swim ashore alone onto a small island. There he watches slaves descend into an underground vault with an ancient, wasted old man (mourned in two brief verse citations on the ravages of age) and provisions, then depart again — without a strikingly beautiful boy they had also brought down. The qalandar digs his own way in and finds the boy: a jeweler’s only son, hidden away from birth on the strength of a horoscope that he will die at fifteen at the hand of a king named ‘Ajib son of Khasib. In a moment he does not share aloud, the qalandar realizes that he himself fired the shot that killed the horseman, and so is that very man; he resolves silently never to harm the boy, and the two live together underground as companions for forty days. On the fortieth, cutting a melon, the qalandar’s foot slips and the knife in his hand kills the boy outright — the horoscope fulfilled by the one man sworn to prevent it. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit. The night is frank about the boy’s death and is translated that way, without euphemism.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الخَامِسَةَ عَشَرَ قٰلَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānat al-laylatu al-khāmisata ʿashar qālat
sentences.l: Now when it was the fifteenth night, she said,
sentences.n: The archive spells "she said" قلت, missing the internal alif of قالت — a defective (Middle Arabic) spelling, not the pronoun "you"; pointed here with a dagger alif (قٰلت) so it reads correctly while the rasm is untouched. This is the standing night-opening formula and will recur unchanged at the head of every night.

sentences.t: بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا المَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ القَرَنْدَلِيَّ الثَّالِثَ قَالَ لِلصَّبِيَّةِ وَالجَمَاعَةُ مُكَتَّفُونَ وَالعَبِيدُ وَاقِفُونَ بِالسُّيُوفِ عَلَى رُؤْسِهِمْ
sentences.tr: balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-qarandalīya al-thālitha qāla li-al-ṣabiyyati wa-al-jamāʿatu mukattafūna wa-al-ʿabīdu wāqifūna bi-al-suyūfi ʿalā ruʾsihim
sentences.l: It has reached me, O happy King, that the third qalandar said to the girl — the company [being] pinioned and the slaves standing with their swords over their heads —
sentences.i: It has reached me, O happy King, that the third qalandar said to the girl, while the whole company sat bound and the slaves stood over them with drawn swords,
sentences.n: The archive prints رؤسهم one wāw short of the full plural رؤوس "heads"; it may be a defective plural spelling, or a collective singular "their head" used loosely for the group. Either way the sense wanted is "over their heads," and that is how it is rendered.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي سَمَّيْتُ اللَّٰهَ وَدَعَوْتُهُ وَ ابْتَهَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَتَعَلَّقْتُ فِى النَّقْرِ الَّذِي فِى الجَبَلِ وَقَدْ تَسَلَّقْتُ فِى الجَبَلِ قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: thumma innī sammaytu Allāha wa-daʿawtuhu wa-ibtahaltu ilayhi wa-taʿallaqtu fī al-naqri alladhī fī al-jabali wa-qad tasallaqtu fī al-jabali qalīlan
sentences.l: Then indeed I pronounced God's name and called on Him and implored Him, and I clung to the cleft that was in the mountain, having already climbed a little way up the mountain,
sentences.i: Then I called on God's name, prayed to Him, and implored Him, and I clung to a cleft in the mountainside, for I had already climbed a little way up it,
sentences.n: "سمّيت الله" is the set phrase for invoking God's name (saying "Bismillāh") before an undertaking, not literally "naming" Him.

sentences.t: فَأَذِنَ اللَّٰهُ أَنْ تَسْكُتَ الرِّيحُ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ وَأَعَانَنِي عَلَى الطُّلُوعِ
sentences.tr: fa-adhina Allāhu an taskuta al-rīḥu fī tilka al-sāʿati wa-aʿānanī ʿalā al-ṭulūʿi
sentences.l: and God gave leave that the wind fall still in that hour, and He helped me in the climbing;
sentences.i: and God allowed the wind to fall still in that hour and helped me up the climb;

sentences.t: فَسَلِمْتُ وَطَلَعْتُ عَلَى الجَبَلِ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ لِي دَرْبٌ إِلَّا القُبَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-salimtu wa-ṭalaʿtu ʿalā al-jabali fa-lam yakun lī darbun illā al-qubbatu
sentences.l: so I came through safely and climbed up onto the mountain, and I had no path except the dome;
sentences.i: so I came through safely and climbed onto the mountain, where I found no way forward except toward the dome;

sentences.t: وَفَرِحْتُ بِسَلَامَتِي غَايَةَ الفَرَحِ فَدَخَلْتُ القُبَّةَ وَتَوَضَّأْتُ وَ صَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ شُكْرًا لِلَّٰهِ عَلَى سَلَامَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥtu bi-salāmatī ghāyata al-faraḥi fa-dakhaltu al-qubbata wa-tawaḍḍaʾtu wa-ṣallaytu rakʿatayni shukran lillāhi ʿalā salāmatī
sentences.l: and I rejoiced at my safety with the utmost joy, and I entered the dome and made ablution and prayed two rak'as in thanks to God for my safety;
sentences.i: and I rejoiced at my deliverance with the utmost joy, entered the dome, performed my ablutions, and prayed two rak'as in thanksgiving to God for my safety;

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي نِمْتُ تَحْتَ القُبَّةِ فَسَمِعْتُ فِي مَنَامِي قَائِلًا يَقُولُ يَا ابْنَ خَضِيبٍ إِذَا انْتَبَهْتَ مِنْ مَنَامِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innī nimtu taḥta al-qubbati fa-samiʿtu fī manāmī qāʾilan yaqūlu yā ibna khaḍībin idhā intabahta min manāmika
sentences.l: Then indeed I slept beneath the dome, and I heard in my sleep a sayer saying: 'O son of Khaḍīb, when you wake from your sleep,'
sentences.i: Then I slept beneath the dome, and in my sleep I heard a voice say: 'O son of Khaḍīb, when you wake from your sleep,'
sentences.n: The archive spells the name خضيب with ḍād here; kept exactly as printed. Note too that the dream addresses the qalandar by this patronymic — a detail whose weight only becomes clear later in the night.

sentences.t: اِحْفِرْ تَحْتَ رِجْلَيْكَ تَجِدْ قَوْسًا مِنْ نُحَاسٍ وَثَلَاثَةَ نُشَّابَاتٍ مِنْ رَصَاصٍ مَنْقُوشَاتٍ عَلَيْهَا طِلَسْمَاتٌ
sentences.tr: iḥfir taḥta rijlayka tajid qawsan min nuḥāsin wa-thalāthata nushshābātin min raṣāṣin manqūshātin ʿalayhā ṭilasmātun
sentences.l: 'Dig beneath your feet — you will find a bow of brass, and three arrows of lead, engraved with talismans upon them,'
sentences.i: 'Dig beneath your feet, and you will find a bow of brass and three leaden arrows, engraved with talismans,'

sentences.t: فَخُذِ القَوْسَ وَالنُّشَّابَ وَارْمِ الفَارِسَ الَّذِي عَلَى القُبَّةِ وَأَرِحِ النَّاسَ مِنْ هَٰذَا البَلَاءِ العَظِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-khudhi al-qawsa wa-al-nushshāba wa-irmi al-fārisa alladhī ʿalā al-qubbati wa-arihi al-nāsa min hādhā al-balāʾi al-ʿaẓīmi
sentences.l: 'so take the bow and the arrows, and shoot the horseman who is on the dome, and give the people rest from this great affliction;'
sentences.i: 'take up the bow and the arrows, shoot the horseman on the dome, and free the people from this great calamity;'

sentences.t: فَإِذَا رَمَيْتَ الفَارِسَ يَقَعُ فِى البَحْرِ وَالقَوْسُ يَقَعُ عِنْدَكَ فَخُذِ القَوْسَ وَادْفِنْهُ فِي مَوْضِعِ القَوْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā ramayta al-fārisa yaqaʿu fī al-baḥri wa-al-qawsu yaqaʿu ʿindaka fa-khudhi al-qawsa wa-idfinhu fī mawḍiʿi al-qawsi
sentences.l: 'When you have shot the horseman, he falls into the sea, and the bow falls by you; then take the bow and bury it in the bow's own place,'
sentences.i: 'Once you have shot the horseman, he will fall into the sea and the bow will fall beside you; take up the bow and bury it in that same spot,'
sentences.n: "in the bow's own place" — that is, back in the very spot beneath his feet where he first dug it up.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا فَعَلْتَ ذَٰلِكَ يَطْفُو البَحْرُ وَيَعْلُو حَتَّى يُسَاوِىَ الجَبَلَ وَ يَطْلُعُ عَلَيْهِ زَوْرَقٌ فِيهِ شَخْصٌ نُحَاسٌ غَيْرُ الَّذِي رَمَيْتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā faʿalta dhālika yaṭfū al-baḥru wa-yaʿlū ḥattā yusāwiya al-jabala wa-yaṭluʿu ʿalayhi zawraqun fīhi shakhṣun nuḥāsun ghayru alladhī ramaytahu
sentences.l: 'When you have done that, the sea rises and swells until it is level with the mountain, and there rises upon it a small boat, in it a figure of brass, other than the one you shot,'
sentences.i: 'Once you have done that, the sea will swell and rise until it stands level with the mountain, and a small boat will come up on it bearing a brazen figure — not the one you shot,'
sentences.n: The archive spells the subjunctive يساوي with a final alif maqṣūra (يساوى) rather than yāʾ — a common interchange of ي/ى in word-final position in Middle Arabic printing. Kept as printed; read and translated as "yusāwiya," "[until it] becomes level with."

sentences.t: يَجِيءُ إِلَيْكَ وَفِي يَدِهِ مِقْذَافٌ فَارْكَبْ مَعَهُ وَلَا تُسَمِّ اللَّٰهَ تَعَالَى فَإِنَّهُ يَتْلَفُ وَيُسَافِرُ بِكَ مُدَّةَ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ إِلَى أَنْ يُوصِلَكَ إِلَى بَحْرِ السَّلَامَةِ
sentences.tr: yajīʾu ilayka wa-fī yadihi miqdhāfun fa-irkab maʿahu wa-lā tusammi Allāha taʿālā fa-innahu yatlafu wa-yusāfiru bika muddata ʿasharati ayyāmin ilā an yūṣilaka ilā baḥri al-salāmati
sentences.l: 'coming toward you, an oar in his hand; so ride with him, and do not name God Most High, for he perishes; and he journeys with you a space of ten days, until he brings you to the Sea of Safety,'
sentences.i: 'coming toward you, an oar in his hand — ride with him, and do not speak the name of God Most High, for if you do he will fail; otherwise he will carry you a ten days' voyage until he brings you to the Sea of Safety,'
sentences.n: A recurring motif in these tales: an enchanted, magically-animated helper is bound by a condition of silence — here, that its rider not speak God's name, on pain of the spell (and the helper) failing.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا وَصَلْتَ هُنَاكَ تَجِدْ مَنْ يُوصِلُكَ إِلَى بَلَدِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā waṣalta hunāka tajid man yūṣiluka ilā baladika
sentences.l: 'and when you arrive there, you will find one who brings you to your own town,'
sentences.i: 'and once you arrive there, you will find someone to carry you on to your own country,'

sentences.t: فَهَٰذَا يَتِمُّ لَكَ إِذَا لَمْ تُسَمِّ اللَّٰهَ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā yatimmu laka idhā lam tusammi Allāha
sentences.l: 'This will be completed for you, if you do not name God.'
sentences.i: 'All this will come to pass for you, provided you do not speak God's name.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اسْتَيْقَظْتُ مِنْ نَوْمِي وَقُمْتُ بِنَشَاطٍ وَفَعَلْتُ مِثْلَمَا قَالَ الهَاتِفُ
sentences.tr: thumma istayqaẓtu min nawmī wa-qumtu bi-nashāṭin wa-faʿaltu mithlamā qāla al-hātifu
sentences.l: Then I woke from my sleep and rose with vigor, and did just as the voice had said,
sentences.i: Then I woke from my sleep, rose briskly, and did exactly as the unseen voice had told me,
sentences.n: الهاتف — "the unseen caller/voice," a stock figure in these tales for a disembodied speaker heard in sleep or in the dark, never seen.

sentences.t: وَضَرَبْتُ الفَارِسَ اَرْمَيْتُهُ فَوَقَعَ فِى البَحْرِ وَقَعَ القَوْسُ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: wa-ḍarabtu al-fārisa armaytuhu fa-waqaʿa fī al-baḥri waqaʿa al-qawsu ʿindī
sentences.l: and I struck the horseman — I shot him — and he fell into the sea; the bow fell by me,
sentences.i: and I struck the horseman — loosed my shot at him — and down he fell into the sea, while the bow dropped at my side,
sentences.n: The archive appears to double the verb here ("I struck the horseman, I-shot-him"), spelling the second verb with an extra, non-etymological alif (ارميته for رَمَيْتُهُ, "I shot him"). Read as an emphatic restatement of the same action rather than an otherwise-unattested verb form; the added alif is a scribal or Middle Arabic feature, not a hamza, so it carries no hamza mark.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ القَوْسَ وَدَفَنْتُهُ فَهَاجَ البَحْرُ وَعَلَا حَتَّى سَاوَى الجَبَلَ وَسَاوَانِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu al-qawsa wa-dafantuhu fa-hāja al-baḥru wa-ʿalā ḥattā sāwā al-jabala wa-sāwānī
sentences.l: So I took the bow and buried it, and the sea surged and rose until it stood level with the mountain — level with me,
sentences.i: So I took up the bow and buried it, and the sea heaved and rose until it stood level with the mountain — level with me,

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَلْبَثْ
sentences.tr: fa-lam albath
sentences.l: and I did not tarry ...
sentences.n: The archived line breaks off here at the edge of this drafting slice, mid-clause (the sentence continues in the next slice: "فلم ألبث أن...", "I had no sooner ... than"); rendered only as far as the text given.

sentences.t: غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ حَتَّى رَأَيْتُ زَوْرَقًا فِي وَسَطِ البَحْرِ قَاصِدًا إِلَى فَحَمِدْتُ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: ghayra sāʿatin ḥattā ra'aytu zawraqan fī wasaṭi al-baḥri qāṣidan ilā fa-ḥamidtu allāha taʿālā
sentences.l: Not an hour, until I saw a skiff in the middle of the sea, heading toward— so I praised God, exalted is He.
sentences.i: Barely an hour had passed before I saw a skiff in the midst of the sea, making its way toward me, and I gave praise to God, exalted is He.
sentences.n: ghayra sāʿatin ḥattā, lit. 'not an hour, until' — an elliptical narrative idiom for 'no sooner had an hour passed than…'. qāṣidan ilā: the archive gives no object for ilā ('toward'); sense, and the parallel phrase below ('heading toward the island'), suggest 'toward me' is meant, but the rasm here supports only plain ilā, so the object is left unstated rather than supplied.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ إِلَى الزَّوْرَقِ فَوَجَدْتُ فِيهِ شَخْصًا مِنَ النُّحَاسِ فِي صَدْرِهِ لَوْحًا مِنَ الرَّصَاصِ مَنْقُوشً بِأَسْمَاءٍ وَطِلَسْمَاتٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala ilā al-zawraqi fa-wajadtu fīhi shakhṣan mina al-nuḥāsi fī ṣadrihi lawḥan mina al-raṣāṣi manqūshan bi-asmā'in wa-ṭilasmātin
sentences.l: Then when it reached the skiff, I found in it a figure of brass, on its chest a tablet of lead, inscribed with names and talismans.
sentences.i: When it drew up to the skiff, I found in it a figure of brass, and on its breast a tablet of lead, engraved with names and talismans.
sentences.n: The subject of 'reached' is left unstated in the Arabic — most naturally the narrator's own craft, or the narrator himself, drawing near; rendered here with an impersonal 'it'. lawḥan and manqūshan continue as further objects of wajadtu, in apposition to shakhṣan.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعْتُ فِى الزَّوْرَقِ وَأَنَا سَاكِتٌ وَلَا أَنْكَلِمُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿtu fī al-zawraqi wa-anā sākitun wa-lā ankalimu
sentences.l: So I boarded the skiff, while I [was] silent and not speaking.
sentences.i: So I climbed into the skiff, keeping silent and not speaking a word.
sentences.n: ankalimu ('I speak') is a Middle Arabic Form VII (infaʿala) usage of the root k-l-m, where Classical would expect Form V atakallamu; it recurs through the tale and is glossed each time rather than corrected. The archive also spells fī ('in') here with alif maqsūra (فى) rather than the usual dotted yāʾ (في) — a spelling variant that recurs through the slice; both are pointed the same way and glossed as the same word.

sentences.t: فَقَذَفَ الشَّخْصُ أَوَّلَ يَوْمٍ وَالثَّانِي وَالثَّالِثَ إِلَى تَمَامِ العَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qadhafa al-shakhṣu awwala yawmin wa-al-thānī wa-al-thālitha ilā tamāmi al-ʿasharati ayyāmin
sentences.l: Then the figure cast [it] the first day, and the second, and the third, until the completion of the ten days.
sentences.i: Then the brazen figure hurled it onward the first day, the second, and the third, until the full ten days were done.
sentences.n: The object of qadhafa ('cast, hurled') is left unstated; sense requires it to be the skiff itself, propelled onward by the brass figure — the same verb qadhafa recurs a few lines on for the sea casting the narrator, and again for the wave casting him ashore, a deliberate repetition worth watching for.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرْتُ وَرَأَيْتُ جَزَائِرَ السَّلَامَةِ فَفَرِحْتُ فَرَحًا عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-naẓartu wa-ra'aytu jazā'ira al-salāmati fa-fariḥtu faraḥan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: Then I looked, and I saw the Isles of Safety, and I rejoiced a great rejoicing.
sentences.i: Then I looked out, and I saw the Isles of Salvation, and I rejoiced with a great joy.
sentences.n: jazā'ir al-salāmah, 'the Isles of Safety/Salvation' — a legendary place-name within the tale's own geography, not a real archipelago.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ شِدَّةِ فَرَحِي ذَكَرْتُ اللَّهَ وَسَمَّيْتُ وَهَلَّلْتُ وَكَبَّرْتُ
sentences.tr: wa-min shiddati faraḥī dhakartu allāha wa-sammaytu wa-hallaltu wa-kabbartu
sentences.l: And from the intensity of my joy, I remembered God, and I said 'In [His] name,' and I said 'There is no god but God,' and I said 'God is greatest.'
sentences.i: And in the intensity of my joy I called God to mind, spoke His name in blessing, proclaimed that there is no god but He, and cried out that God is greatest.
sentences.n: sammaytu, hallaltu, kabbartu name three set devotional formulas (the basmala, the tahlīl 'lā ilāha illā allāh', and the takbīr 'Allāhu akbar') by the verb for uttering them — a common shorthand rather than a literal 'I named / declared-one / magnified'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ قَذَفَنِي الزَّوْرَقُ فِى البَحْرِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ وَانْقَلَبَ فِى البَحْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faʿaltu dhālika qadhafanī al-zawraqu fī al-baḥri thumma rajaʿa wa-inqalaba fī al-baḥri
sentences.l: Then when I did that, the skiff cast me into the sea; then it turned back and overturned in the sea.
sentences.i: But no sooner had I done that than the skiff flung me into the sea, then turned back and capsized in the waves.

sentences.t: فَكُنْتُ أَعْرِفُ العَوْمَ فَعُمْتُ ذَلِكَ اليَوْمَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-kuntu aʿrifu al-ʿawma fa-ʿumtu dhālika al-yawma ilā al-layli
sentences.l: And I knew swimming, so I swam that day until the night.
sentences.i: Now, I knew how to swim, and so I swam that whole day until nightfall.

sentences.t: فَخَذَلَتْ سَوَاعِدِي وَكَلَّتْ أَكْتَافِي وَتَعِبْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-khadhalat sawāʿidī wa-kallat aktāfī wa-taʿibtu
sentences.l: Then my forearms failed, and my shoulders grew weary, and I grew tired.
sentences.i: Then my arms gave out, my shoulders grew weary, and I was overcome with exhaustion.

sentences.t: بَقِيتُ فِى الهَلَكَاتِ ثُمَّ تَشَهَّدْتُ وَأَيْقَنْتُ بِالمَوْتِ
sentences.tr: baqītu fī al-halakāti thumma tashahhadtu wa-ayqantu bi-al-mawti
sentences.l: I remained in perils; then I made my profession of faith and became certain of death.
sentences.i: I remained in mortal peril, until at last I spoke my profession of faith, certain that death had come for me.

sentences.t: فَهَاجَ البَحْرُ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الرِّيَاحِ فَجَاءَتْ مَوْجَةٌ كَالقَلْعَةِ العَظِيمَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-hāja al-baḥru min kathrati al-riyāḥi fa-jā'at mawjatun ka-al-qalʿati al-ʿaẓīmati
sentences.l: Then the sea raged from the abundance of the winds, and there came a wave like the great fortress.
sentences.i: Then the sea grew wild with the fury of the winds, and a wave came on like a great citadel.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلَتْنِي وَقَذَفَتْنِي قَذْفَةً صِرْتُ فَوْقَ البَرِّ بِمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamalatnī wa-qadhafatnī qadhfatan ṣirtu fawqa al-barri bi-mā yurīdu allāhu
sentences.l: So it carried me and cast me a casting; I found myself upon the shore, by what God willed.
sentences.i: It swept me up and hurled me forward in a single cast, and by God's will I found myself upon dry land.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعْتُ البَرَّ وَعَصَرْتُ ثِيَابِي وَنَشَّفْتُهَا وَنَشَرْتُهَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَبِتُّ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿtu al-barra wa-ʿaṣartu thiyābī wa-nashshaftuhā wa-nashartuhā ʿalā al-arḍi wa-bittu
sentences.l: So I went up onto the land, and I wrung out my clothes, and I dried them, and I spread them on the ground, and I passed the night.
sentences.i: So I climbed onto dry land, wrung out my clothes, dried them, and laid them out on the ground, and there I spent the night.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَتُ لَبِسْتُ أَثْوَابِي وَقُمْتُ أَنْظُرُ أَيْنَ أَمْشِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥtu labistu athwābī wa-qumtu anẓuru ayna amshī
sentences.l: Then when I entered the morning, I put on my garments and I rose, looking [to see] where I might walk.
sentences.i: When morning came, I dressed myself, and I got up to see where I might go.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ غُوطَةً فَجِئْتُهَا وَدُرْتُ حَوْلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu ghūṭatan fa-jiʾtuhā wa-durtu ḥawlahā
sentences.l: Then I found a hollow, so I came to it and went around it.
sentences.i: Then I came upon a leafy hollow, so I went to it and walked around it.
sentences.n: ghūṭah, lit. a fertile, tree-lined depression (as in al-Ghūṭah, the oasis around Damascus); here simply a wooded hollow on the island.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ المَوْضِعَ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ جَزِيرَةً صَغِيرَةً وَالبَحْرُ مُحِيطٌ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu al-mawḍiʿa alladhī anā fīhi jazīratan ṣaghīratan wa-al-baḥru muḥīṭun bihā
sentences.l: Then I found the place that I was in [to be] a small island, the sea surrounding it.
sentences.i: Then I discovered that the place I was in was a small island, with the sea surrounding it on every side.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ كُلَّمَا أَخْلُصُ مِنْ بَلِيَّةٍ أَقَعُ فِي أَعْظَمَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu kullamā akhluṣu min baliyyatin aqaʿu fī aʿẓama minhā
sentences.l: So I said, 'Every time I escape a calamity, I fall into a greater one than it.'
sentences.i: So I said to myself, 'Every time I win free of one calamity, I fall into a still greater one.'

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا مُتَفَكِّرٌ فِي أَمْرِي وَأَنَا أَتَمَنَّى المَوْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā mutafakkirun fī amrī wa-anā atamannā al-mawta
sentences.l: And while I [was] pondering over my situation, and I [was] wishing for death—
sentences.i: And while I sat pondering my situation, longing for death—

sentences.t: وَإِذَا نَظَرْتُ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ مَرْكَبًا فِيهِ نَاسٌ قَاصِدًا إِلَى الجَزِيرَةِ الَّتِي أَنَا فِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā naẓartu min baʿīdin markaban fīhi nāsun qāṣidan ilā al-jazīrati allatī anā fīhā
sentences.l: And when I looked, from a distance, [there was] a ship, in it people, heading toward the island that I [was] in.
sentences.i: And when I looked, I made out in the distance a ship with people aboard, making for the very island I was on.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَقَعَدْتُ عَلَى شَجَرَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-qaʿadtu ʿalā shajaratin
sentences.l: So I got up and sat upon a tree.
sentences.i: So I got up and climbed into a tree.
sentences.n: qaʿadtu ʿalā shajaratin, lit. 'I sat upon a tree' — idiomatic for climbing up and perching in it, to watch unseen.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالمَرْكَبِ قَدِ الْتَصَقَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-markabi qad iltaṣaqa
sentences.l: And behold, [there] with the ship, [it] had already stuck fast.
sentences.i: And there, all at once, was the ship — it had already run aground.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, 'and behold, there was…' — the idhā of surprise, which introduces what suddenly appears rather than a clause of time (contrast the temporal idhā just above); iltaṣaqa (lit. 'stuck fast, clung') here means the ship had come to rest against the shore.

sentences.t: وَطَلَعَ إِلَى البَرِّ مِنْهُ عَشَرَةُ عَبِيدٍ وَمَعَهُمْ مَسَاحِي
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalaʿa ilā al-barri minhu ʿasharatu ʿabīdin wa-maʿahum masāḥī
sentences.l: And there went up onto the shore from it ten slaves, and with them [were] mattocks.
sentences.i: And ten slaves came ashore from it, carrying mattocks with them.
sentences.n: masāḥī ('mattocks, spades') keeps its yāʾ here where Classical case-grammar would drop it in this position (an indefinite nominative manqūṣ plural, masāḥin); Middle Arabic frequently treats such tool-plurals as an invariable form, and it is vocalised as it stands rather than corrected.

sentences.t: وَمَشَوْا إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى وَسَطِ الجَزِيرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-mashaw ilā an waṣalū ilā wasaṭi al-jazīrati
sentences.l: And they walked until they arrived at the middle of the island.
sentences.i: They walked on until they reached the middle of the island.

sentences.t: فَحَفَرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَكَشَفُوا عَنْ طَابِقٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥafarū fī al-arḍi wa-kashafū ʿan ṭābiqin
sentences.l: And they dug in the ground, and they uncovered a slab.
sentences.i: They dug into the ground and uncovered a stone trapdoor.
sentences.n: ṭābiq here denotes a flagstone or trapdoor set into the ground, covering the mouth of an underground vault — not its later sense of 'storey, floor'.

sentences.t: فَشَالُوا الطَّابِقَ وَفَتَحُوا بَابَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-shālū al-ṭābiqa wa-fataḥū bābahu
sentences.l: And they lifted the slab and opened its door.
sentences.i: They lifted the slab away and opened its door.
sentences.n: shālū 'they lifted' is a Middle Arabic/colloquial verb (shāla, yashīlu, 'to lift, carry') rather than the Classical ḥamala or rafaʿa; it recurs in the tale and is glossed rather than corrected.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ عَادُوا إِلَى المَرْكَبِ وَنَقَلُوا مِنْهَا خُبْزًا وَدَقِيقًا وَسَمْنًا وَعَسَلًا وَأَغْنَامًا وَآلَاتٍ مَا يَحْتَاجُ السَّاكِنُ
sentences.tr: thumma ʿādū ilā al-markabi wa-naqalū minhā khubzan wa-daqīqan wa-samnan wa-ʿasalan wa-aghnāman wa-ālātin mā yaḥtāju al-sākinu
sentences.l: Then they returned to the ship, and they carried from it bread, and flour, and clarified butter, and honey, and sheep, and tools [of] what the dweller needs.
sentences.i: Then they went back to the ship and unloaded from it bread, flour, clarified butter, honey, livestock, and whatever tools and goods the one who was to live there would need.
sentences.n: The list itemizes provisions for the vault's occupant — the old man introduced in the next lines — in the rhythm typical of the tale's inventories.

sentences.t: وَالعَبِيدُ طَالِعِينَ نَازِلِينَ إِلَى المَرْكَبِ وَهُمْ يُحَوِّلُونَ مِنَ المَرْكَبِ وَيَنْزِلُونَ إِلَى أَنْ نَقَلُوا جَمِيعَ مَا فِى المَرْكَبِ إِلَى الحُفْرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ʿabīdu ṭāliʿīna nāzilīna ilā al-markabi wa-hum yuḥawwilūna mina al-markabi wa-yanzilūna ilā an naqalū jamīʿa mā fī al-markabi ilā al-ḥufrati
sentences.l: And the slaves, going up and down to the ship, they transferring from the ship and going down [again], until they had carried everything that [was] in the ship to the pit.
sentences.i: The slaves went back and forth to the ship, ferrying the goods from it and going down again, until they had carried everything in the ship down into the pit.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ طَلَعَ العَبِيدُ وَ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika ṭalaʿa al-ʿabīdu wa-
sentences.l: Then after that the slaves came up, and—
sentences.i: Then after that the slaves came up, and—
sentences.n: The archived line breaks off here mid-clause (the conjunction 'wa-' with nothing following); the sentence continues in the next slice, presumably introducing the old man's appearance.

sentences.t: مَعَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ أَحْسَنُ مَا يَكُونُ وَفِي وَسَطِهِمْ شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ قَدْ أَبْقَى مَا بَقِيَ وَعَرَكَهُ الدَّهْرُ وَاِسْتَبْقَى كَأَنَّهُ مُفْنًي مُلْقًى فِي خِرْقَةِ زُرْقَةٍ تَمُرُّ فِيهَا الْأَرْيَاحُ غَرْبًا وَشَرْقًا كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: maʿahum thiyābun aḥsanu mā yakūnu wa-fī wasaṭihim shaykhun kabīrun qad abqā mā baqiya wa-ʿarakahu al-dahru wa-istabqā ka-annahu mufnan mulqan fī khirqati zurqatin tamurru fīhā al-aryāḥu gharban wa-sharqan kamā qāla fīhi al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: With them [were] clothes, the finest there could be; and in their midst, a great old man who had kept-remaining what remained [of him] — time had rubbed him down, and-yet-he-endured — as though he were a spent-thing, cast into a rag-of-blueness through which the winds pass, westward and eastward, as the poet said of him:
sentences.i: With them came garments finer than any could be, and among them an old man of great age, reduced to whatever of him yet remained — time had ground him down, and yet he lingered on — as though he were a thing spent to nothing, flung into a tattered blue rag through which the winds blew, west and east, as the poet said of him:
sentences.n: خِرْقَةِ زُرْقَةٍ, lit. 'a rag of blueness', is an iḍāfa of description standing in for the expected feminine adjective زرقاء ('blue'); rendered 'a rag-of-blueness' in the literal layer, 'a tattered blue rag' idiomatically. وَاسْتَبْقَى is ambiguous between transitive 'preserved/spared [something]' and, as taken here, intransitive 'lingered on, endured'.

sentences.t:
قَدْ أَرْعَشَ الدَّهْرُ ايّ رَعْشٍ * وَالدَّهْرُ ذُو قُوَّةٍ وَبَطْشٍ
قَدْ كُنْتُ أَمْشِي وَلَسْتُ أَعْيَى * وَالْيَوْمَ أَعْيَى وَلَسْتُ أَمْشِي
sentences.tr:
qad arʿasha al-dahru ayya raʿshin * wa-al-dahru dhū quwwatin wa-baṭshin
qad kuntu amshī wa-lastu aʿyā * wa-al-yawma aʿyā wa-lastu amshī
sentences.l:
Time indeed has shaken [him] — what a shaking! * for time is possessed of strength and violence.
I used to walk and not tire, * and today I am tired and cannot walk.
sentences.i:
Time indeed has shaken him — what a shaking! For time holds strength and violence in its grip.
I used to walk and never tire; today I tire, and I cannot walk.
sentences.n: ايّ (for Classical أَيّ, 'what a—!') is printed here without its expected initial hamza and with no vowelling beyond the shadda; kept exactly as the archive gives it, per the rule that pointed verse is copied as printed.

sentences.t: وَيْلَ الشَّيْخِ فِي يَدِ صَبِيٍّ وَهُوَ قَدْ أُفْرِغَ فِي قَالَبِ الجَمَالِ وَالبَهَاءِ وَ الكَمَالِ حَتَّى أَنَّهُ يُضْرَبُ بِحُسْنِهِ الأمْثَالُ وَهُوَ كَالقَضِيبِ الرَّطِيبِ يَسْحَرُ كُلَّ قَلْبٍ بِجَمَالِهِ وَيَسْلُبُ كُلَّ لُبٍّ بِدَلَالِهِ كَمَا قَٰلَ فِيهِ الشَّاعِرُ حَيْثُ
sentences.tr: wayla al-shaykhi fī yadi ṣabiyyin wa-huwa qad ufrigha fī qālabi al-jamāli wa-al-bahāʾi wa-al-kamāli ḥattā annahu yuḍrabu bi-ḥusnihi al-amthālu wa-huwa ka-al-qaḍībi al-raṭībi yasḥaru kulla qalbin bi-jamālihi wa-yaslubu kulla lubbin bi-dalālihi kamā qāla fīhi al-shāʿiru ḥaythu
sentences.l: Woe [is] the old man's, in the hand of a boy! And he had been poured into the mold of beauty, and splendor, and perfection, until proverbs are struck by his beauty, and he is like the moist twig, bewitching every heart with his beauty and stealing every mind with his coyness, as the poet said of him, saying:
sentences.i: Alas for the old man, now in a mere boy's hand! For that boy had been cast in the very mold of beauty, splendor, and perfection, until proverbs were coined for his beauty — he was like a tender green branch, bewitching every heart with his loveliness and stealing away every mind with his coy charm, as the poet said of him:
sentences.n: يُضْرَبُ بِحُسْنِهِ الْأَمْثَالُ: the idiom يُضرَب بـ...المثل, lit. 'a proverb is struck by means of...', means 'X becomes proverbial, a byword is coined for X'. قٰلَ here spells قَالَ defectively (قل, no alif); pointed with the dagger alif (ٰ) on the ق, as the convention requires.

sentences.t:
جِيءَ بِالحُسْنِ كَيْ يُقَايِسَهُ * فَنَكَّسَ الحُسْنُ رَأْسَهُ خَجَلًا
فَقِيلَ يَا حُسْنُ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ كَذَا * فَقَالَ أَمَا كَذَا رَأَيْتُ فَلَا
sentences.tr:
jīʾa bi-al-ḥusni kay yuqāyisahu * fa-nakkasa al-ḥusnu raʾsahu khajalan
fa-qīla yā ḥusnu hal raʾayta kadhā * fa-qāla amā kadhā raʾaytu fa-lā
sentences.l:
Beauty was brought, that it might be compared against him, * and Beauty bowed its head, out-of-shame.
Then it was said, 'O Beauty, have you seen the like of this?' * and he said, 'Indeed, the like of this I have not seen — no.'
sentences.i:
Beauty itself was brought to be measured against him, and Beauty bowed its head in shame.
Then they said, 'O Beauty, have you ever seen the like of this?' And Beauty answered, 'Truly, the like of this I have never seen — never.'
sentences.n: Beauty (الْحُسْن) is personified here as a rival brought to be judged against the boy, addressed directly and answering in the first person. أَمَا in the second line is taken as an emphatic particle ('indeed'); the exact force of this terse reply is uncertain.

sentences.t: فَيَا سَيِّدَتِي لَمْ يَزَالُوا مَاشِينَ حَتَّى أَتَوْا إِلَى الطَّابَقِ وَنَزَلُوا الْجَمِيعُ فِي الطَّابَقِ وَغَابُوا سَاعَةً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-yā sayyidatī lam yazālū māshīn ḥattā ataw ilā al-ṭābaq wa-nazalū al-jamīʿ fī al-ṭābaq wa-ghābū sāʿatan aw akthar
sentences.l: So, O my lady, they did-not-cease walking until they came to the vault, and they all went down into the vault, and they were-gone an hour or more.
sentences.i: So, my lady, on they walked until they reached the vault, and all of them went down into it, and were gone an hour or more.
sentences.n: الطَّابَق here is an underground vault/chamber reached by a stair or shaft, not the modern sense 'floor, story'; the word recurs through this passage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَلَعُوا الْعَبِيدُ وَالشَّيْخُ وَلَمْ يَطْلَعِ الصَّبِيُّ مَعَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭalaʿū al-ʿabīd wa-al-shaykh wa-lam yaṭlaʿi al-ṣabī maʿahum
sentences.l: Then came-up the slaves and the old man, and the boy did not come up with them.
sentences.i: Then the slaves and the old man came up, but the boy did not come up with them.
sentences.n: طَلَعُوا takes full plural agreement though it precedes a compound subject — classical usage normally leaves such a preposed verb singular, but full agreement is an attested (if minority) pattern, not an error.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَدُّوا بَابَ الطَّابَقِ كَمَا كَانَ وَنَزَلُوا فِي الْمَرْكَبِ وَغَابُوا عَنْ عَيْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma raddū bāb al-ṭābaq kamā kāna wa-nazalū fī al-markab wa-ghābū ʿan ʿaynī
sentences.l: Then they put back the door of the vault as it had been, and went down into the ship, and were-gone from my eye.
sentences.i: Then they closed the door of the vault as it had been, went down into the ship, and vanished from my sight.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهُوا قُمْتُ وَنَزَلْتُ مِنْ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ وَمَشَيْتُ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ الرَّدْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā tawajjahū qumtu wa-nazaltu min ʿalā al-shajarah wa-mashaytu ilā mawḍiʿ al-radm
sentences.l: So when they had set off, I got up and climbed-down from atop the tree, and walked to the place of the earth-mound.
sentences.i: So when they had gone their way, I got up and climbed down from the tree, and walked to the place of the buried mound.
sentences.n: الرَّدْم: earth heaped up to conceal something — here, the mound covering the vault's trapdoor.

sentences.t: وَنَبَشْتُ التُّرَابَ وَنَقَلْتُهُ وَطَوَّلْتُ رُوحِي حَتَّى شِلْتُ جَمِيعَ التُّرَابِ فَانْكَشَفَ الطَّابَقُ
sentences.tr: wa-nabashtu al-turāb wa-naqaltuhu wa-ṭawwaltu rūḥī ḥattā shiltu jamīʿ al-turāb fa-inkashafa al-ṭābaq
sentences.l: And I dug up the earth and carried it off, and I prolonged my soul (labored on) until I had carried-away all the earth, and the vault lay uncovered.
sentences.i: And I dug up the earth and cleared it away, laboring on until I had carried off all the earth, and the vault lay uncovered.
sentences.n: شِلْتُ is the colloquial-flavored verb شَالَ/يَشِيل 'to carry, lift, remove', beside Classical حَمَلَ; it recurs below (شِلْتُهَا).

sentences.t: فَإِذَا هُوَ خَشَبٌ وَسِعَ فِلْقَةَ حَجَرِ الطَّاحُونِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā huwa khashabun wasiʿa filqata ḥajar al-ṭāḥūn
sentences.l: And behold, it (was) wood that held a piece of the millstone.
sentences.i: And there it was — a wooden cover, just large enough to hold a piece of the millstone.
sentences.n: فَإِذَا here is the 'idhā of surprise', introducing a sudden discovery ('and behold...'); it need not be followed by بِـ.

sentences.t: فَشِلْتُهَا فَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهَا سُلَّمٌ عُقَلٌ عُقَلٌ فَتَعَجَّبْتُ لِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-shiltuhā fa-bāna min taḥtihā sullamun ʿuqalun ʿuqalun fa-taʿajjabtu li-dhālika
sentences.l: So I lifted it away, and there appeared, from beneath it, a ladder, joint-upon-joint, and I marveled at that.
sentences.i: So I lifted it aside, and beneath it a staircase came into view, close-jointed throughout, and I marveled at it.
sentences.n: عُقَل عُقَل is an obscure, possibly corrupt reduplication; taken here as 'joint upon joint' (عُقْلَة, a joint/knot, as of a jointed cane), describing a tightly-fitted staircase — though the doubling may instead be a colloquial intensifier ('very sturdy'). The reading is uncertain.

sentences.t: وَنَزَلْتُ فِي السُّلَّمِ حَتَّى انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazaltu fī al-sullam ḥattā intahaytu ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: And I went down onto the ladder until I reached its end.
sentences.i: And I climbed down the staircase until I reached the bottom.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ بُنْيَانًا نَظِيفًا مَفْرُوشًا بِأَنْوَاعِ الْبُسُطِ وَالْحَرِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu bunyānan naẓīfan mafrūshan bi-anwāʿi al-busuṭ wa-al-ḥarīr
sentences.l: And I found a building, clean, spread with kinds of carpets and silk.
sentences.i: And I found a clean chamber, spread with every kind of carpet and silk.

sentences.t: وَالصَّبِيُّ جَالِسٌ عَلَى مَرْتَبَةٍ عَالِيَةٍ مُتَّكِئٌ عَلَى مِدْوَرَةٍ فِي يَدِهِ مِرْوَحَةٌ وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مَشْمُومٌ وَرَيَاحِينُ وَهُوَ وَحْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ṣabī jālisun ʿalā martabatin ʿāliyatin muttakiʾun ʿalā midwaratin fī yadihi mirwaḥatun wa-bayna yadayhi mashmūmun wa-rayāḥīnu wa-huwa waḥdahu
sentences.l: And the boy (was) sitting upon a high cushion, leaning upon a round-bolster, in his hand a fan, and before him a fragrant-nosegay and sweet-basil, and he alone.
sentences.i: And the boy sat upon a raised cushion, leaning against a round bolster, a fan in his hand, and before him a nosegay and sprigs of sweet basil, and he was quite alone.
sentences.n: مِدْوَرَة: a round cushion or bolster; مَشْمُوم: a bunch of fragrant herbs held to the nose, a nosegay.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي اصْفَرَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī iṣfarra
sentences.l: And when he saw me, he turned pale
sentences.i: And when he saw me, he turned pale

sentences.t: أَوٰنُهُ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: awānuhu fa-sallamtu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: his time (had come) — so I greeted him
sentences.i: So when the moment came, I greeted him,
sentences.n: The archive's رسم here (اونه) has no room for the medial alif of أوان ('a time, a moment'); read as a defective spelling completing a sentence begun before this slice (perhaps '...until his time/moment came'), with the dropped long vowel restored as a dagger alif on the wāw, per the house convention for defective spellings (cf. قَٰلَ for قال). The clause this completes lies outside the slice and cannot be verified from it.

sentences.t: وَ فَاتَ لَهُ طَمِّنْ رَوْعَكَ وَ هُدَّ رَوْعَكَ لَا بَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-fāta lahu: ṭammin rawʿaka wa-hudda rawʿaka lā baʾsa ʿalayka
sentences.l: and it passed to him [i.e. I said to him]: 'set your fright at rest and quash your fright, there is no harm upon you,'
sentences.i: and I said to him, 'Set your heart at ease — put your fright to rest; no harm shall come to you.
sentences.n: فات له 'and it passed to him' is an odd bridge into direct speech where 'so I said to him' is expected; kept as printed rather than silently read as قال. طَمِّنْ روعك و هُدَّ روعك doubles the same idea (calm your fright — quash your fright), a sajʿ-like exhortation; هُدَّ is the imperative of هَدَّ ('break/quash'), not هَدِّئْ, since the rasm (هد) has no seat for a final hamza.

sentences.t: أَنَا إِنْسِيٌّ مِثْلُكَ اِبْنُ مَلِكٍ سَاقَتْنِي الْمَقَادِيرُ إِلَيْكَ أُونِسُكَ عَلَى وَحْدِكَ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: anā insiyyun mithluka ibnu malikin sāqatnī al-maqādīru ilayka ūnisuka ʿalā waḥdika fīhā
sentences.l: I am human like you, a king's son; the decrees have driven me to you, [that] I may keep-you-company, on your own-ness, in it
sentences.i: I am a human being like you, the son of a king; fate has driven me to you, that I might keep you company in your solitude here.
sentences.n: على وحدك here carries its idiomatic sense 'on your own, by yourself' rather than a literal 'upon your solitude'.

sentences.t: قِصَّتُكَ وَ مَا حِكَايَتُكَ حَتَّى سَكَنْتَ تَحْتَ الْأَرْضِ وَحْدَكَ
sentences.tr: qiṣṣatuka wa-mā ḥikāyatuka ḥattā sakanta taḥta al-arḍi waḥdaka
sentences.l: your story, and what is your tale, that you have dwelt beneath the earth alone?
sentences.i: Now tell me your story — what is your tale, that you have come to live beneath the earth all alone?

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقَ أَنِّي مِنْ جِنْسِهِ فَرِحَ وَ رَدَّ لَوْنُهُ وَ قَرَّبَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَ قَالَ يَا أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqa annī min jinsihi fariḥa wa-radda lawnuhu wa-qarrabanī ilayhi wa-qāla yā akhī
sentences.l: and when he was assured that I was of his own kind, he rejoiced, and his color returned, and he drew me near to him, and said, 'O my brother,'
sentences.i: When he was certain that I was human, like him, he rejoiced; the color came back to his face, and he drew me close, and said, 'My brother,'

sentences.t: قِصَّتِي عَجِيبَةٌ وَ ذَٰلِكَ أَنَّ وَالِدِي تَاجِرٌ جَوْهَرِيٌّ لَهُ تِجَارَةٌ وَ عَبِيدٌ وَ مَمَالِيكُ تُجَّارٌ يُسَافِرُونَ لَهُ فِى الْمَرَاكِبِ بِالتِّجَارَاتِ إِلَى أَقْصَى الْبِلَادِ وَ لَهُمْ جِمَالَاتٌ وَ أَمْوَالٌ مُتَّسِعَةٌ
sentences.tr: qiṣṣatī ʿajībatun wa-dhālika anna wālidī tājirun jawharīyun lahu tijāratun wa-ʿabīdun wa-mamālīku tujjārun yusāfirūna lahu fī al-marākibi bi-al-tijārāti ilā aqṣā al-bilādi wa-lahum jimālātun wa-amwālun muttasiʿatun
sentences.l: My story is strange; and that is that my father was a jewel-merchant, he had trade, and slaves, and merchant-mamluks who traveled for him on the ships with the goods to the farthest of the lands, and they had camels and ample wealth,
sentences.i: My story is a strange one. My father was a jewel-merchant, a man of trade, with slaves and mamluk agents who sailed the ships on his behalf, carrying goods to the farthest lands; they had camel-trains and vast wealth,

sentences.t: وَ لَمْ يُرْزَقْ وَلَدًا قَطُّ فَرَأَى فِي مَنَامِهِ أَنَّهُ يُرْزَقُ وَلَدًا فِي عُمُرِهِ قِصَرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yurzaq waladan qaṭṭu fa-raʾā fī manāmihi annahu yurzaqu waladan fī ʿumurihi qiṣarun
sentences.l: and he had never been granted a child at all; then he saw in his dream that he would be granted a child, in whose lifetime [there was] shortness,
sentences.i: yet he had never once been given a child. Then, in a dream, he saw that a son would be given to him — a son whose life would be short.
sentences.n: عمره قصر is compressed: 'in his lifetime, shortness', i.e. a short-lived son; read قِصَر as the noun (shortness), predicate of an implied 'his lifespan would have'.

sentences.t: فَأَصْبَحَ وَالِدِي فِي صَرِيخٍ وَ بُكَاءٍ
sentences.tr: fa-aṣbaḥa wālidī fī ṣarīkhin wa-bukāʾin
sentences.l: so my father came to be in crying-out and weeping,
sentences.i: So my father fell to wailing and weeping.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْقَابِلَةُ عَلِقَتْ وَالِدَتِي بِي فَأَرَّخَ تَارِيخَ حَبَلِهَا وَ انْقَضَتْ أَيَّامُهَا فَوَلَدَتْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānat al-laylatu al-qābilatu ʿaliqat wālidatī bī fa-arrakha tārīkha ḥabalihā wa-inqaḍat ayyāmuhā fa-waladatnī
sentences.l: and when the following night came, my mother conceived me, and he dated the date of her pregnancy, and her days elapsed, and she bore me,
sentences.i: Then, the very next night, my mother conceived me; my father noted down the date of her conception, and when her time was fulfilled, she gave birth to me.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ وَالِدِي وَ أَوْلَمَ الْوَلَائِمَ وَ أَطْعَمَ الْفُقَرَاءَ وَ الْمَسَاكِينَ لِكَوْنِهِ رُزِقَ بِي فِي آخِرِ عُمُرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa wālidī wa-awlama al-walāʾima wa-aṭʿama al-fuqarāʾa wa-al-masākīna li-kawnihi ruziqa bī fī ākhiri ʿumurihi
sentences.l: so my father rejoiced, and held the wedding-feasts, and fed the poor and the destitute, for his being granted me at the end of his life,
sentences.i: My father rejoiced greatly; he held great feasts and fed the poor and the destitute, since he had been given me so late in his life.

sentences.t: فَجَمَعَ الْمُنَجِّمِينَ وَ أَهْلَ التَّقَاوِيمِ وَ حُكَمَاءَ الزَّمَانِ وَ أَصْحَابَ التَّوَارِيخِ وَ الْمَوَالِيدِ فَكَشَفُوا إِلَى مِيلَادِي
sentences.tr: fa-jamaʿa al-munajjimīna wa-ahla al-taqāwīmi wa-ḥukamāʾa al-zamāni wa-aṣḥāba al-tawārīkhi wa-al-mawālīdi fa-kashafū ilā mīlādī
sentences.l: so he gathered the astrologers, and the people of the almanacs, and the sages of the age, and the masters of chronicles and nativities, and they uncovered [the stars] unto my birth,
sentences.i: He gathered together the astrologers, the makers of almanacs, the wise men of the age, and the masters of chronicles and horoscopes, and they cast his eye over the stars of my birth,
sentences.n: كشفوا إلى ميلادي: 'كَشَفَ' (to examine/uncover, an astrologer's casting of a horoscope) ordinarily governs عَلَى or the bare accusative; the Middle Arabic text here uses إلى instead — a preposition swap kept as printed, first of a few in this slice.

sentences.t: وَ قَالُوا لَهُ وَلَكَ يَعِيشُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً وَ عَلَيْهِ قَطْعٌ فِيهَا إِنْ سَلِمَ مِنْهَا عَاشَ زَمَانًا طَوِيلًا
sentences.tr: wa-qālū lahu wa-laka yaʿīshu khamsata ʿashara sanatan wa-ʿalayhi qaṭʿun fīhā in salima minhā ʿāsha zamānan ṭawīlan
sentences.l: and they said to him: 'And your (son) will live fifteen years, and upon him a cutting-off is in it; if he survives it, he will live a long time,'
sentences.i: and they told him: 'Your son will live fifteen years, and a fatal crisis hangs over him within that span; if he escapes it, he will live long,'

sentences.t: وَ سَبَبُ مَوْتِهِ أَنَّ فِي بَحْرِ الْهَلَكَاتِ جَبَلُ الْمِغْنَاطِيسِ عَلَيْهِ فَارِسٌ وَ فَرَسٌ مِنْ نُحَاسٍ
sentences.tr: wa-sababu mawtihi anna fī baḥri al-halakāti jabalu al-mighnāṭīsi ʿalayhi fārisun wa-farasun min nuḥāsin
sentences.l: and the cause of his death [is] that in the Sea of Perils [there is] a mountain of lodestone, upon it a horseman and a horse of brass,
sentences.i: The cause of his death would be this: in the Sea of Perils stands a mountain of lodestone, and upon it a horseman and a horse of brass,

sentences.t: وَ الْفَارِسُ فِي صَدْرِهِ لَوْحٌ مِنْ رَصَاصٍ مَتَى وَقَعَ الْفَارِسُ مِنْ عَلَى فَرَسِهِ بَعْدَ خَمْسِينَ يَوْمًا يَمُوتُ وَلَدُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-fārisu fī ṣadrihi lawḥun min raṣāṣin matā waqaʿa al-fārisu min ʿalā farasihi baʿda khamsīna yawman yamūtu waladuka
sentences.l: and the horseman, in his chest [is] a tablet of lead; whenever the horseman falls from off his horse, after fifty days your son will die,
sentences.i: and the horseman bears on his chest a tablet of lead. Whenever that horseman falls from his horse — fifty days later — your son will die,

sentences.t: وَ قَاتِلُهُ هُوَ الَّذِي يَرْمِى الْفَارِسَ مَلِكٌ اسْمُهُ عَجِيبُ بْنُ خَضِيبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qātiluhu huwa alladhī yarmī al-fārisa malikun ismuhu ʿajību bnu khaḍībin
sentences.l: and his killer is the one who shoots the horseman: a king, his name [is] 'Ajib, son of Khadib,
sentences.i: and his slayer will be the one who shoots down that horseman — a king named 'Ajib, son of Khadib.'
sentences.n: The father's name for the king here (خضيب) is spelled differently a few lines below (خصيب); both are kept exactly as printed. See the note at that later occurrence.

sentences.t: فَاغْتَمَّ أَبِي غَمًّا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-ightamma abī ghamman shadīdan
sentences.l: so my father grieved with a violent grief,
sentences.i: So my father grieved a grief most bitter.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّهُ رَبَّانِي وَ أَحْسَنَ تَرْبِيَتِى إِلَى أَنْ بَلَغْتُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: thumma annahu rabbānī wa-aḥsana tarbiyatī ilā an balaghtu khamsata ʿashara sanatan
sentences.l: then he raised me and made excellent my upbringing, until I reached fifteen years,
sentences.i: Then he raised me and gave me the finest upbringing, until I turned fifteen.

sentences.t: وَ مِنْ مُدَّةِ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ جَاءَ لِأَبِي الْخَبَرُ أَنَّ الْفَارِسَ وَقَعَ فِى الْبَحْرِ وَ الَّذِي رَمَاهُ اسْمُهُ عَجِيبُ بْنُ الْمَلِكِ خَصِيبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-min muddati ʿasharati ayyāmin jāʾa li-abī al-khabaru anna al-fārisa waqaʿa fī al-baḥri wa-alladhī ramāhu ismuhu ʿajību bnu al-maliki khaṣībin
sentences.l: and from a space of ten days, the news came to my father that the horseman had fallen into the sea, and the one who shot him, his name [is] 'Ajib, son of King Khasib,
sentences.i: Then, ten days ago, word reached my father that the horseman had fallen into the sea, and that the one who had shot him down was named 'Ajib, son of King Khasib.
sentences.n: The father's name is spelled خصيب here, against خضيب a few lines above (U15) — kept as printed both times; likely simple scribal inconsistency rather than two different men.

sentences.t: فَخَافَ عَلَيَّ أَبِي مِنَ الْقَتْلِ فَنَقَلَنِي إِلَى هَٰذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-khāfa ʿalayya abī min al-qatli fa-naqalanī ilā hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: so my father feared for me, from being killed, so he moved me to this place,
sentences.i: So my father, fearing I would be killed, moved me to this place —

sentences.t: وَ هَٰذِهِ قِصَّتِي وَ سَبَبُ وَحْدَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi qiṣṣatī wa-sababu waḥdatī
sentences.l: and this is my story, and the cause of my solitude.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ قِصَّتَهُ تَعَجَّبْتُ وَ قُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي أَنَا الَّذِي عَمِلْتُ هَٰذَا كُلَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu qiṣṣatahu taʿajjabtu wa-qultu fī nafsī anā alladhī ʿamiltu hādhā kullahu
sentences.l: and when I heard his story, I was amazed, and I said within myself: 'I am the one who did all of this,'
sentences.i: When I heard his story, I was struck with wonder, and I said to myself: 'I am the very one who has done all this!'

sentences.t: وَ أَنَا وَ اللَّهِ لَا أَقْتُلُهُ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-anā wa-allāhi lā aqtuluhu abadan
sentences.l: and I, by God, I will never kill him,
sentences.i: And I — by God — will never kill him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُلْتُ يَا مَوْلَايَ كُفِيتَ الدَّاءَ وَ الرَّدَى
sentences.tr: thumma qultu yā mawlāya kufīta al-dāʾa wa-al-radā
sentences.l: then I said: 'O my master, you have been spared the affliction and the ruin,'
sentences.i: Then I said to him: 'Master, you have been spared the sickness and the ruin.'
sentences.n: كُفِيتَ الداء والردى: passive 'you have been sufficed against/spared', taking الداء والردى as the things warded off, a set idiomatic pairing (affliction / ruin).

sentences.t: وَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَا تَرَى هَمًّا وَلَا غَمًّا وَلَا تَشْوِيشًا
sentences.tr: wa-in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā lā tarā hamman wa-lā ghamman wa-lā tashwīshan
sentences.l: and if God, Most High, wills, you will see no worry, and no grief, and no confusion,
sentences.i: and, God willing, you shall know no worry, no grief, and no distress.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَقْعُدُ عِنْدَكَ وَ أَخْدُمُكَ وَأَرْجِعُ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِي بَعْدَ أَنْ أُونِسُكَ فِي هَٰذِهِ الْأَيَّامِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā aqʿudu ʿindaka wa-akhdumuka wa-arjiʿu ilā ḥāli sabīlī baʿda an ūnisuka fī hādhihi al-ayyāmi
sentences.l: and I will sit with you, and serve you, and return to the state of my way, after that I keep-you-company in these days,
sentences.i: As for me, I will stay with you and wait on you, and afterward — once I have kept you company these few days — I will go my own way again,

sentences.t: تُوصِلُنِي إِلَى بَعْضِ الْمَمَالِيكِ أُسَافِرُ مَعَهُمْ إِلَى بِلَادِي
sentences.tr: tūṣilunī ilā baʿḍi al-mamālīki usāfiru maʿahum ilā bilādī
sentences.l: you convey me to some of the mamluks, [that] I travel with them to my country,
sentences.i: so that you may help me reach some of the traveling mamluks, and I may journey with them back to my own country.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْتُ أُحَدِّثُهُ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-jalastu uḥadithuhu ilā al-layli
sentences.l: and I sat, conversing-with-him, until the night,
sentences.i: And I sat conversing with him until nightfall.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ أَوْقَدْتُ شَمْعَةً كَبِيرَةً وَعَمَّرْتُ الْقَنَادِيلَ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu awqadtu shamʿatan kabīratan wa-ʿammartu al-qanādīla
sentences.l: then I rose, [and] lit a large candle, and I tended the lamps,
sentences.i: Then I got up, lit a great candle, and tended to the lamps,

sentences.t: وَ جَلَسْنَا بَعْدَ أَنْ مَدَّيْنَا شَيْئًا مِنَ الْأَكْلِ فَأَكَلْنَا
sentences.tr: wa-jalasnā baʿda an maddaynā shayʾan min al-akli fa-akalnā
sentences.l: and we sat, after we had spread-out something of the food, and we ate,
sentences.i: We sat together, and once we had spread out some food, we ate,
sentences.n: مدّينا/مديت (here and in U30) are Middle Arabic forms of the doubled verb مدّ, 'to spread/lay out', treated as if weak-final (مَدَّى/مَدَّيْنَا) rather than the classical مَدَدْنَا; kept as pronounced/printed.

sentences.t: وَقُمْتُ مَدَّيْتُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْحَلَاوَةِ فَتَحَلَّيْنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qumtu maddaytu shayʾan min al-ḥalāwati fa-taḥallaynā
sentences.l: and I rose, [and] spread-out something of the sweets, and we had-dessert,
sentences.i: then I got up and set out some sweets, and we had our dessert,

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْنَا نُحَدِّثُ بَعْضُنَا حَتَّى ذَهَبَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ أَكْثَرُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasnā nuḥadithu baʿḍunā ḥattā dhahaba min al-layli aktharuhu
sentences.l: and we sat, we conversed [with] one another, until most of the night had gone by,
sentences.i: and we sat talking with one another until the greater part of the night had passed;

sentences.t: فَنَامَ فَغَطَّيْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-nāma fa-ghaṭṭaytuhu
sentences.l: then he slept, and I covered him,
sentences.i: then he fell asleep, and I covered him over,

sentences.t: وَقُمْتُ أَنَا نِمْتُ
sentences.tr: wa-qumtu anā nimtu
sentences.l: and I rose, I [too] slept,
sentences.i: and I in turn lay down and slept.
sentences.n: وقمت أنا نمت juxtaposes two verbs without a connective in a way classical style avoids; read as 'and I, for my part, lay down and slept' — a Middle Arabic paratactic construction.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحْتُ قُمْتُ وَسَخَّنْتُ قَلِيلًا مِنْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥtu qumtu wa-sakhkhantu qalīlan min
sentences.l: and when I awoke, I rose, and I warmed a little of…
sentences.i: And when morning came, I rose and warmed a little of...
sentences.n: The unit breaks off mid-clause at the edge of the slice (قليلا من...); the object continues in the following slice.

sentences.t: اَلْمَاءَ وَنَبَّهْتُهُ بِرِفْقٍ فَاسْتَيْقَظَ
sentences.tr: al-māʾa wa-nabbahtuhu bi-rifqin fa-istayqaẓa
sentences.l: ...the water; and I roused him gently, and he awoke,
sentences.n: This slice opens mid-sentence: 'the water' is the trailing object of a verb from the previous slice (most likely 'I heated the water'); 'him' is the sick young man the qalandar has been tending in the underground vault.

sentences.t: فَأنَيْتُهُ بِالْمَاءِ الْمُسَخَّنِ فَغَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʾānaytuhu bi-al-māʾ al-musakhkhan fa-ghasala wajhahu
sentences.l: and I brought him with the heated water, and he washed his face,
sentences.i: then I brought him the warmed water, and he washed his face,
sentences.n: 'فأنيته' is textually obscure. It is read here as a form-IV verb built on ء-ن-ي/و-ن-ي ('to bring something once it is ready'), though it may instead be a slip for فأتيته, 'I came to him with' (the verb أتى بـ, 'to bring', used just below in the ruling); the translation follows the sense, not a confident etymology.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَ جُزِيتَ خَيْرًا يَا فَتَى
sentences.tr: wa-qāla juzīta khayran yā fatā
sentences.l: and he said, 'You have been rewarded with good, O young man!'
sentences.i: and he said, 'God reward you well, young man!'

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ مَتَى سَلِمْتُ مِنَ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ وَ مِنَ الَّذِي اسْمُهُ عَجِيبُ بْنُ خَصِيبٍ خَلَّيْتُ أَبِي يُكَافِئُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-allāhi matā salimtu min alladhī anā fīhi wa-min alladhī ismuhu ʿAjību bnu Khaṣībin khallaytu abī yukāfiʾuka
sentences.l: 'and, by God, whenever I am safe from that which I am in, and from the one whose name is ʿAjib son of Khaṣib, I will let my father reward you,'
sentences.i: 'and by God, once I am free of this danger, and of the one named ʿAjib son of Khaṣib, I will have my father reward you,'
sentences.n: The boy is unknowingly naming the qalandar himself: it was the qalandar who shot the brass horseman in the earlier adventure, fulfilling the very role of 'ʿAjib son of Khaṣib' that will end the boy's life.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا إِذَا مُتَّ فَالسَّلَامُ مِنِّي عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā idhā muttu fa-al-salāmu minnī ʿalayka
sentences.l: 'but if I die, then the farewell is from me upon you,'
sentences.i: 'but if I die, then farewell to you from me,'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَا كَانَ يَوْمًا يُصِيبُكَ فِيهِ شَرٌّ وَجَعَلَ اللَّهُ يَوْمِي قَبْلَ يَوْمِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā kāna yawman yuṣībuka fīhi sharrun wa-jaʿala Allāhu yawmī qabla yawmika
sentences.l: and I said to him, 'Let there not be a day in which harm befalls you, and may God set my day before your day,'
sentences.i: and I said to him, 'May no day ever bring you harm, and may God take me before He takes you,'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَدَّمْتُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْأَكْلِ فَأَكَلْنَا وَعَمِلْتُ لَهُ بَخُورًا فَطَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma qaddamtu shayʾan min al-akl fa-akalnā wa-ʿamiltu lahu bakhūran fa-ṭāba
sentences.l: then I set out something of the food, and we ate; and I made incense for him, and it grew fragrant,
sentences.i: then I set out some food and we ate, and I burned incense for him until the air was sweet,

sentences.t: وَصَنَعْتُ لَهُ مِنْقَلَةً وَلَعِبْتُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣanaʿtu lahu minqalatan wa-laʿibtu anā wa-iyyāhu
sentences.l: and I made him a game-board, and I played, I and he,
sentences.i: and I made him a board for a game, and he and I played together,

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَكَلْنَا شَيْئًا مِنَ الْحَلَاوَةِ وَلَعِبْنَا إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma akalnā shayʾan min al-ḥalāwa wa-laʿibnā ilā al-layl
sentences.l: then we ate something of the sweets, and we played until the night,
sentences.i: then we ate some sweetmeats, and played on until nightfall,

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ أَوْقَدْتُ الْمَصَابِيحَ وَقَدَّمْتُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْأَكْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu awqadtu al-maṣābīḥ wa-qaddamtu shayʾan min al-akl
sentences.l: then I got up, lit the lamps, and set out something of the food,
sentences.i: then I rose, lit the lamps, and brought out food again,

sentences.t: وَقَعَدْتُ أُحَدِّثُهُ إِلَى أَنْ بَقِيَ شَيْءٌ قَلِيلٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَنَامَ وَغَطَّيْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qaʿadtu uḥaddithuhu ilā an baqiya shayʾun qalīlun min al-layl fa-nāma wa-ghaṭṭaytuhu
sentences.l: and I sat talking with him until a little of the night remained, and he slept, and I covered him,
sentences.i: and I sat and talked with him until only a little of the night was left; then he slept, and I covered him,

sentences.t: وَ نِمْتُ وَلَمْ أَزَلْ يَا سَيِّدَتِي أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ
sentences.tr: wa-nimtu wa-lam azal yā sayyidatī ayyāman wa-layāliya
sentences.l: and I slept; and I did not cease, O my lady, for days and nights,
sentences.i: and slept myself. And so it went on, my lady, for days and nights,
sentences.n: 'O my lady' addresses Sitt al-Ḥusn, the qalandar's listener within the frame of 'The Porter and the Three Ladies' — a reminder that this whole adventure is a tale being told aloud.

sentences.t: وَبَقِيَ لَهُ فِي قَلْبِي مَحَبَّةٌ وَسَلَوْتُ هَمِّي
sentences.tr: wa-baqiya lahu fī qalbī maḥabbatun wa-salawtu hammī
sentences.l: and there remained for him in my heart love, and my worry was consoled,
sentences.i: love for him settled into my heart, and my fear was soothed,

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي كَذَبَ الْمُنَجِّمُونَ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَقْتُلُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu fī nafsī kadhaba al-munajjimūn wa-allāhi lā aqtuluhu
sentences.l: and I said to myself, 'The astrologers lied — by God, I will not kill him,'
sentences.i: and I told myself, 'The astrologers were wrong — by God, I will never harm him,'

sentences.t: وَ لَمْ أَزَلْ أَخْدُمُهُ وَأُنَادِمُهُ وَأُحَادِثُهُ إِلَى تِسْعَةٍ وَثَلٰثِينَ يَوْمًا وَلَيْلَةَ الْأَرْبَعِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal akhdumuhu wa-unādimuhu wa-uḥādithuhu ilā tisʿatin wa-thalāthīna yawman wa-laylat al-arbaʿīn
sentences.l: and I did not cease serving him, and keeping him company, and conversing with him, up to thirty-nine days and the night of the fortieth,
sentences.i: and I went on serving him, keeping him company, and talking with him, for thirty-nine days, until the night of the fortieth,

sentences.t: فَرِحَ الصَّبِيُّ وَقَالَ يَا أَخِي الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي نَجَّانِي مِنَ الْمَوْتِ
sentences.tr: fariḥa al-ṣabiyyu wa-qāla yā akhī al-ḥamdu lillāhi alladhī najjānī min al-mawt
sentences.l: the boy rejoiced and said, 'O my brother, praise be to God, who has saved me from death,'
sentences.i: the boy was overjoyed and said, 'O my brother, praise God, who has saved me from death,'

sentences.t: وَهٰذَا بِبَرَكَتِكَ وَبَرَكَةِ قُدُومِكَ وَأَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يَرُدَّكَ إِلَى بَلَدِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā bi-barakatika wa-barakat qudūmika wa-asʾalu Allāha an yaruddaka ilā baladika
sentences.l: 'and this is by your blessing and the blessing of your coming; and I ask God that He return you to your country,'
sentences.i: 'and this is by your blessing, and by the blessing of your coming; and I pray God to bring you safely home,'

sentences.t: وَلٰكِنْ يَا أَخِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تُسَخِّنَ لِي مَاءً أَغْتَسِلُ وَأَغْسِلُ جَسَدِي
sentences.tr: wa-lākin yā akhī urīdu an tusakhkhina lī māʾan aghtasil wa-aghsil jasadī
sentences.l: 'but, O my brother, I want you to heat water for me, so that I may bathe and wash my body,'
sentences.i: 'but, my brother, I want you to heat some water for me, so I can bathe and wash myself,'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً وَسَخَّنْتُ لَهُ مَاءً بِكَثْرَةٍ وَدَخَلْتُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu ḥubban wa-karāmatan wa-sakhkhantu lahu māʾan bi-kathratin wa-dakhaltu bihi ʿalayhi
sentences.l: and I said, 'With love and honor,' and I heated for him water in abundance, and went in to him with it,
sentences.i: and I said, 'Gladly, with all my heart' — and heated him plenty of water, and carried it in to him,
sentences.n: 'Ḥubban wa-karāmatan', literally 'as love and as honor', is a set phrase of willing assent, roughly 'gladly, with pleasure.'

sentences.t: وَغَسَلْتُ جَسَدَهُ غَسْلًا جَيِّدًا بِلَا قَلَقٍ وَدَلَكْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ghasaltu jasadahu ghaslan jayyidan bilā qalaqin wa-dalaktuhu
sentences.l: and I washed his body a good washing, without haste, and I rubbed him down,
sentences.i: and I washed his body thoroughly and unhurriedly, and rubbed him down,

sentences.t: وَخَلَعْتُهُ وَغَيَّرْتُ لَهُ أَثْوَابً
sentences.tr: wa-khalaʿtuhu wa-ghayyartu lahu athwāban
sentences.l: and I stripped him, and I changed garments for him,
sentences.i: and undressed him and put fresh clothes on him,

sentences.t: وَ فَرَشْتُ تَحْتَهُ فَرْشًا عَالِيًا
sentences.tr: wa-farashtu taḥtahu farshan ʿāliyan
sentences.l: and I spread beneath him a raised bedding,
sentences.i: and spread beneath him a fine, soft bed,

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ الصَّبِيُّ وَاسْتَلْقَى عَلَيْهِ وَنَامَ مِنَ الِاسْتِحْمَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa al-ṣabiyyu wa-istalqā ʿalayhi wa-nāma min al-istiḥmām
sentences.l: and the boy came and lay back upon it, and slept from the bathing,
sentences.i: and the boy came and lay down on it, falling asleep from the bath,

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَ يَا أَخِي اقْطَعْ لَنَا بِطِّيخَةً وَذَوِّبْ بِهَا سُكَّرَ نَبَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā akhī iqṭaʿ lanā biṭṭīkhatan wa-dhawwib bihā sukkar nabātin
sentences.l: and he said, 'O my brother, cut for us a melon, and melt into it some rock-candy,'
sentences.i: and he said, 'My brother, cut us a melon, and melt some sugar-candy into it,'
sentences.n: The archive spells 'he said' defectively here as قل, missing its long vowel; it is pointed قَٰلَ, with a dagger alif, rather than by inserting an alif into the rasm.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْتُ الْخِزَانَةَ فَلَقِيتُ بِطِّيخَةً مَلِيحَةً وَوَجَدْتُهَا فِي طَبَقٍ فَكَسَرْتُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-dakhaltu al-khizāna fa-laqītu biṭṭīkhatan malīḥatan wa-wajadtuhā fī ṭabaqin fa-kasartuhā
sentences.l: so I went into the storeroom, and I came upon a fine melon, and found it on a tray, and I broke it open,
sentences.i: so I went into the pantry and found a fine melon on a tray, and cracked it open,

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ يَا سَيِّدِي مَا عِنْدَكَ سِكِّينٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu yā sayyidī mā ʿindaka sikkīnun
sentences.l: and I said, 'O my master, do you have a knife?'
sentences.i: and I said, 'My lord, do you have a knife?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَا هِيَ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي عَلَى هٰذِهِ الصِّفَةِ الْعَالِيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hā hiya fawqa raʾsī ʿalā hādhihi al-ṣiffati al-ʿāliya
sentences.l: and he said, 'Here it is, above my head, on that high shelf,'
sentences.i: and he said, 'There it is, above my head, on that high shelf,'
sentences.n: 'الصفة' here is a raised ledge or shelf, not 'description' or 'attribute' — its more usual modern sense.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَنَا مُسْتَعْجِلٌ فَأَخَذْتُ السِّكِّينَ وَمَسَكْتُهَا مِنْ نِصَالِهَا وَرَجَعْتُ إِلَى خَلْفِي
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-anā mustaʿjilun fa-akhadhtu al-sikkīna wa-masaktuhā min niṣālihā wa-rajaʿtu ilā khalfī
sentences.l: so I got up, in haste, and took the knife, and gripped it by its blade, and turned back,
sentences.i: so I got up quickly, took the knife, but gripped it by the blade, and turned back,
sentences.n: Gripping the blade rather than the handle is the detail that makes the coming accident possible.

sentences.t: فَعَثَرَتْ رِجْلِي وَانْبَطَشْتُ عَلَى الصَّبِيِّ وَالسِّكِّينُ فِي يَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿatharat rijlī wa-inbaṭashtu ʿalā al-ṣabiyyi wa-al-sikkīnu fī yadī
sentences.l: and my foot stumbled, and I pitched down upon the boy, the knife in my hand,
sentences.i: and my foot caught, and I pitched forward onto the boy, the knife still in my hand,

sentences.t: فَشَرَعَتِ السِّكِّينُ بِمَا كُتِبَ فِي الْأَزَلِ وَانْغَرَزَتْ فِي قَلْبِ الصَّبِيِّ فَمَاتَ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-sharaʿat al-sikkīnu bimā kutiba fī al-azal wa-inghazarat fī qalb al-ṣabiyyi fa-māta min sāʿatihi
sentences.l: and the knife went, by what was written in eternity, and plunged into the boy's heart, and he died on the instant,
sentences.i: and the knife — by what had been written from all eternity — drove into the boy's heart, and he died at once,
sentences.n: 'الأزل', pre-eternity, names the eternal divine decree: the very prophecy the boy fled underground to escape is fulfilled by the one hand sworn never to harm him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَضَى نَحْبَهُ وَعَلِمْتُ أَنِّي قَتَلْتُهُ صَرَخْتُ صَرْخَةً عَظِيمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaḍā naḥbahu wa-ʿalimtu annī qataltuhu ṣarakhtu ṣarkhatan ʿaẓīmatan
sentences.l: and when he had fulfilled his vow, and I knew that I had killed him, I cried out a great cry,
sentences.i: and when he had breathed his last, and I knew that it was I who had killed him, I let out a terrible cry,
sentences.n: 'قضى نحبه', literally 'fulfilled his vow', is a Qur'anic euphemism (33:23) for dying, used here of the boy.

sentences.t: وَلَطَمْتُ عَلَى وَجْهِي وَشَقَيْتُ أَثْوَابِي
sentences.tr: wa-laṭamtu ʿalā wajhī wa-shaqaytu athwābī
sentences.l: and I struck my face, and I tore my garments,
sentences.i: and struck my face and tore my clothes,
sentences.n: 'Tore' (شقيت) is spelled here as if from a weak root; the classical spelling of 'I tore' would be شَقَقْتُ, from the doubled root ش-ق-ق — a Middle Arabic leveling kept exactly as printed.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu innā lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūn
sentences.l: and I said, 'We belong to God, and to Him we are returning,'
sentences.i: and I cried, 'We belong to God, and to Him we return,'
sentences.n: The formula of Qur'an 2:156 (the istirjāʿ), spoken on hearing of a death or calamity.

sentences.t: يَا مُسْلِمُونَ هٰذَا الصَّبِيُّ بَقِيَ لَهُ مِنَ الْقَطْعِ الَّذِي خَبَّرُوا بِهِ الْمُنَجِّمُونَ وَالْحُكَمَاءُ إِلَى الْأَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا لَيْلَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ
sentences.tr: yā muslimūn hādhā al-ṣabiyyu baqiya lahu min al-qaṭʿ alladhī khabbarū bihi al-munajjimūn wa-al-ḥukamāʾ ilā al-arbaʿīn yawman laylatun wāḥidatun
sentences.l: 'O Muslims, this boy — there remained to him, of the allotted term the astrologers and the wise men had told of, until the fortieth day, one night,'
sentences.i: 'O believers, this boy — of the span the astrologers and the wise men had foretold, only one night remained until the fortieth day,'
sentences.n: 'القطع', literally 'the cutting', here means the allotted term or portion of life decreed for him.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَجَلُ هٰذَا الْمَلِيحِ عَلَى يَدِي
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ajalu hādhā al-malīḥi ʿalā yadī
sentences.l: 'and the appointed death of this handsome one was by my hand,'
sentences.i: 'and this beautiful boy's death has come by my own hand!'

sentences.t: فَيَا لَيْتَنِي مِنْ قَبْلُ لَمْ أَقْطَعْ هٰذِهِ الْبِطِّيخَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-yā laytanī min qablu lam aqṭaʿ hādhihi al-biṭṭīkhata
sentences.l: 'would that I had not, before, cut this melon,'
sentences.i: 'would that I had never cut this melon!'

sentences.t: مَا هٰذَا إِلَّا مَصَائِبُ وَ غُصَصٌ
sentences.tr: mā hādhā illā maṣāʾibu wa-ghuṣaṣun
sentences.l: 'this is nothing but calamities and chokings,'
sentences.i: 'this is nothing but calamity heaped on calamity,'

sentences.t: وَلٰكِنْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا
sentences.tr: wa-lākin li-yaqḍiya Allāhu amran kāna mafʿūlan
sentences.l: 'but, that God might accomplish a matter that was already done,'
sentences.i: 'but it is only that God should bring to pass a thing already decreed,'
sentences.n: Echoes the Qur'anic phrase (8:42), 'amran kāna mafʿūlan', 'a matter that was destined to be done.'

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalām al-mubāḥ
sentences.l: and morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from the speech permitted [to her],
sentences.i: and morning overtook Shahrazad, so she fell silent, and left unsaid what more she had to tell,
sentences.n: The standard night-ending formula, repeated with only the night's number changing throughout the work.
